text:
Predicates:
BornInMultipleBirth(x) ::: x is born in a multiple birth.
SiblingsBornTogether(x) ::: x has siblings who were born together.
SpendTime(x) ::: x spends a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings.
Complain(x) ::: x complains often about annoying siblings.
LiveAtHome(x) ::: x lives at home.
LiveWithStrangers(x) ::: x lives with strangers.
Baby(x) ::: x is a baby.

Premises:
∀x (BornInMultipleBirth(x) → SpendTime(x)) ::: People who are born in a multiple birth with siblings spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings.
∀x (SiblingsBornTogether(x) → BornInMultipleBirth(x)) ::: If people have siblings who were born together, then they were born in a multiple birth.
∀x (Complain(x) → SiblingsBornTogether(x)) ::: If people complain often about annoying siblings, then they have siblings who were born together.
∀x (LiveAtHome(x) → ¬LiveWithStrangers(x)) ::: If people live at home, then they do not live with strangers.
∀x (SpendTime(x) → LiveAtHome(x)) ::: If people spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings, then they often live at home.
(Baby(luke) ∧ BornInMultipleBirth(luke) ∧ LiveWithStrangers(luke)) ⊕ ¬(Baby(luke) ∨ BornInMultipleBirth(luke) ∨ LiveWithStrangers(luke)) ::: Luke either is a baby born in a multiple birth and lives with strangers, or is not a baby born in a multiple birth and does not live with strangers.

Conclusion:
¬BornInMultipleBirth(luke) ∧ ¬Complain(luke) ::: Luke is neither born in a multiple birth nor complains often about annoying siblings.
